solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Action wanes roughly — as does reaction, say I! (5,6)

annotation.definition: Action wanes roughly — as does reaction, say I!

indicatorNotes.roughly: done roughly, the letters come out in a rough, rearranged order

annotation.surface: A physicist boasting of his own law: push on something and it pushes back just as hard.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the answer: Newton's third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction, so as action wanes, so does reaction.
annotation.definitionFit: The 'I' who states that action and reaction are equal and opposite is Isaac Newton.

entries.clue: Island redeveloped units occupying original position (2,4)

indicatorNotes.redeveloped: something redeveloped is rebuilt in a new layout

blocks.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

annotation.surface: Housing units on an island are rebuilt on the same spot they always stood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Redeveloped units' reads as a property phrase, which hides the rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for 'in its original place'.

entries.clue: Ancient king a problem getting on top of male film director (6,9)

indicatorNotes.getting on top of: in a down clue, what sits on top comes first

blocks.note: Alfred the Great, ninth-century king of Wessex
a cock is a male bird

annotation.surface: An old king and his troubles loom over a man, like a scene from a period drama.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down entry the king and the problem stack above the male, which is the only sense 'getting on top of' has here.
annotation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock directed Psycho, Vertigo and The Birds.

entries.clue: Meat and potato dish’s restriction around extravagant, irrational cuisine, finally (7,3)

indicatorNotes.around: a cage physically surrounds whatever it holds, so CAGE goes around OTT
indicatorNotes.finally: only the final letter of 'cuisine' is used

annotation.surface: A food critic complains that rules are strangling an over-the-top, illogical kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like a comment on the cooking; it is the maths sense, a number like pi that is not a fraction. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is minced beef topped with mashed potato.

entries.clue: Regular placements in setting a heating device (4)

indicatorNotes.Regular placements in: take letters at regular intervals from what follows

blocks.note: the even letters of sEtTiNg A

annotation.surface: Instructions for placing a heater at regular intervals around a room.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is not the volcano: an etna is also a small spirit burner for heating liquids.
annotation.definitionFit: An etna is a small spirit lamp used to heat water or food.

entries.clue: Time in support repeatedly including advanced discussion (4-1-4)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another: T sits inside TEE
indicatorNotes.including: the two copies include A between them

blocks.note: T (time) inside TEE, a golf support

annotation.surface: Talking over a period of backing, again and again, with progress made.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' signals copying, not movement: the first chunk is used twice, with A between.
annotation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people.

entries.clue: Sign of agreement not on the cards, limiting bishop for certain (2,5)

indicatorNotes.limiting: OUT closes in on B from both sides

annotation.surface: A card player's agreement that a bishop is certainly not in the deck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not on the cards' sounds like a card game; it just means ruled out, OUT.
annotation.definitionFit: 'No doubt' means certainly.

entries.clue: Noted detective’s later course (7,4)

blocks.note: dick is slang for a detective

annotation.surface: A famous sleuth's next step in his career.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Noted' pretends to mean famous; it means seen. Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants, so 'later course' is dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: A pudding comes later in the meal than the main course.

entries.clue: Who might be excited by a sport etc? (9)

annotation.definition: Who might be excited by a sport etc?
annotation.surface: A question about who gets worked up watching games.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a spectator is the one excited by sport, and the letters of A SPORT ETC, excited, make the word.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue describes a spectator, the person sport is staged to excite.

entries.clue: Broadcasting manner? No going back on that (2,3)

indicatorNotes.going back: going back means travelling in reverse, so the letters are read from the end
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, ON sits on top of AIR

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
an air is a manner, as in 'an air of confidence'

annotation.surface: A presenter's style, and a refusal to back down on it.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'manner' tempts you to read it as the definition; it gives AIR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a programme that is broadcasting is live on the airwaves.

entries.clue: Description of noblemen seizing river as proof of ownership (5,4)

indicatorNotes.seizing: TITLED grabs DEE and holds it inside

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Scotland and on the England–Wales border

annotation.surface: Aristocrats grab a river and claim it as their property.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Description of noblemen' asks for an adjective, not a noun like PEERS: noblemen are described as titled.
annotation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document proving who owns land.

entries.clue: Something to entertain expert on board, maybe with period not otherwise arranged (12)

indicatorNotes.otherwise arranged: the letters of NOT are put in another order

blocks.note: a springboard diver; 'maybe' flags an example

annotation.surface: Laying on a party for a chess master or board-game champion who has time to spare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expert on board' suggests chess or a company director; it is someone on a diving board.
annotation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light piece of music written to entertain; the name means 'diversion'.

entries.clue: Seize pence, breaking into international bank (7)

indicatorNotes.breaking into: P forces its way inside MOUND

blocks.note: a bank of earth is a mound

annotation.surface: A bank robbery: grab the pennies by breaking into a global bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the earth kind, not the money kind the surface wants.
annotation.definitionFit: To impound is to seize and hold, as police impound a car.

entries.clue: Child with hunger, upset in disposition (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns YEN upside down

annotation.surface: A hungry child in a bad mood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the child's temper; in a down entry it flips YEN to NEY. Kidney as 'temperament' survives in 'of the same kidney'.
annotation.definitionFit: Kidney is an old word for temperament or kind, as in 'men of that kidney'.

entries.clue: Security device, iron, beside river, installed during part of weekend (6,3)

indicatorNotes.beside: 'beside' means next to, so FE is set right alongside TYNE
indicatorNotes.installed during: FE and TYNE are put inside SAT

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the Tyne, the river at Newcastle

annotation.surface: A security system with an iron frame is put up by a river over the weekend.
annotation.walkthrough: Two pieces go into one weekend day, so the day ends up split around them. The Tyne is the river through Newcastle.
annotation.definitionFit: A safety net catches you if you fall, literally or financially.

entries.clue: Peter out to get actors in shape, under pressure? (3-4)

blocks.note: to peter out is to die away
the actors in a play are its cast

annotation.surface: A director's worry: the show fizzles unless the actors are whipped into shape under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In shape, under pressure' sounds like fitness or stress; die-casting forces molten metal into a mould under pressure.
annotation.definitionFit: Die-cast metal is shaped by forcing it into a mould under pressure.

entries.clue: Very quiet in support, not forceful (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another: P sits inside AID

annotation.surface: Someone who supports you very quietly, never pushing.
annotation.walkthrough: P sits inside AID, and V goes in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Vapid means flat and lacking force or spirit.

entries.clue: Rough garment keeping a long time (6)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so TOG holds ERA inside

blocks.note: a tog is an item of clothing, as in 'togs'
an era is a long period

annotation.surface: A coarse garment that has lasted for years.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like an adjective describing the garment; it is a noun, a rough, a thug. Toerag is British slang for a scoundrel.
annotation.definitionFit: A toerag is a contemptible lout, and a rough is a thuggish person.

entries.clue: Storm surrounding first-class pillar (8)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so BLUSTER encloses A

blocks.note: to storm is to bluster, rage noisily

annotation.surface: A tempest raging round a top-quality column.
annotation.walkthrough: A goes after the B: B(A)LUSTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short pillars supporting a handrail.

entries.clue: United’s second defeat in middle of week, travelling (2,5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another: N and ROUT sit inside EE

blocks.note: the middle two letters of wEEk
a rout is a heavy defeat

annotation.surface: A football report: Manchester United lose again in a midweek away game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'United's second defeat' reads as a football result; it is a letter and a word, and 'middle of week' takes two letters because week has four.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: French for 'on the way', so someone travelling is en route.

entries.clue: Means to get in uniform, likewise worn by English navy (8)

indicatorNotes.worn by: SAME wears ERN, holding it inside like clothing

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: How to join up: get into uniform, just as English sailors wear it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Means to get in uniform' reads as a recruiting line; the definition stops at 'get in', a way of logging in.
annotation.definitionFit: A username is what you enter to log in to a system.

entries.clue: Drunk’s loss of paperwork in gale? (5,6,2,3,4)

blocks.note: read literally: three sheets of paper blown away

annotation.surface: A tipsy office worker lets his papers blow away in a storm.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from sailing, where a sheet is a rope; the second definition pretends sheets are paper.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Three sheets to the wind' is an idiom for very drunk.

entries.clue: Style of delivery outshines leg (7)

annotation.surface: A bowler whose delivery is better than a leg-side ball.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' and 'leg' both sound like cricket, but 'leg' is just a limb, a pin.
annotation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward spin put on a ball when it is bowled or hit.

entries.clue: Problem in comprehending former lover – lady is baffled about that (8)

indicatorNotes.baffled: baffled letters are thrown into confusion
indicatorNotes.about: the scrambled letters go around EX

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

annotation.surface: A woman can't understand her ex, and is baffled by it.
annotation.walkthrough: EX goes inside DYSL...IA, the rearranged LADY IS.
annotation.definitionFit: Dyslexia is a difficulty in reading and interpreting words.

entries.clue: Church leader welcoming one instrument maker (7)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: a host welcoming a guest takes them in, so LUTHER takes I inside

blocks.note: Martin Luther, who led the Reformation

annotation.surface: A church leader greets a craftsman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Church leader' suggests a bishop or pope; it is the Reformation leader Martin Luther.
annotation.definitionFit: A luthier makes stringed instruments such as violins and lutes.

entries.clue: Literature including book about covering of Toscanini’s opera texts (8)

indicatorNotes.including: to include is to hold within, so LIT holds B and RE

annotation.surface: A study of Toscanini's books on opera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering of' asks for the outside letters, the first and last. Toscanini was a famous opera conductor, which is why the surface fits.
annotation.definitionFit: Libretti (plural of libretto) are the words of operas.

entries.clue: Say a lot of nonsense about love — it’s a boost to the self (3,4)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of TRIPE, missing its last letter
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so EG...TRIP wraps around O

blocks.note: TRIPE, nonsense, without its last letter
love = nil = O, as in tennis

annotation.surface: Someone talking rubbish about love, just to feel good about themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: The two outer pieces wrap round love, so O lands in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done to boost your own self-importance.

entries.clue: Source of oil, as it happens (5)

annotation.definition: Source of oil, as it happens

indicatorNotes.Source of: the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

annotation.surface: Where oil comes from, as it happens.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, 'source of oil' is O and 'as it happens' is LIVE; read straight, the whole clue is a plain fact about the olive.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the olive is, as it happens, a source of oil, since olive oil is pressed from the fruit.

entries.clue: Attempt to absorb article after article from Berlin about nutrition (7)

indicatorNotes.to absorb: to absorb is to soak something up inside yourself, so TRY takes A in
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means coming later, so T(A)RY is placed behind DIE

annotation.surface: A German food writer attempts article after article on nutrition.
annotation.walkthrough: Two different articles: A in English, DIE in German.
annotation.definitionFit: Dietary means relating to diet and nutrition.

entries.clue: Conflicting sources confused with passport (2,5-8)

indicatorNotes.confused: something confused is jumbled, so the letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: Contradictory information muddled up with someone's passport details.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two fodder words.
annotation.definitionFit: People at cross-purposes are working against each other by misunderstanding.

entries.clue: Scientist starts to boast of his research (4)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starting letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Boast Of His Research

annotation.surface: A scientist beginning to show off about his work.
annotation.walkthrough: Niels Bohr, the Danish physicist who modelled the atom.
annotation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was a Nobel Prize-winning physicist.

entries.clue: Those hoping for returns from US incline to follow intelligence about America (8)

annotation.definition: Those hoping for returns from US
annotation.definitionNote: the definition names the people; the answer is the list they are on

indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come behind, so LIST goes after W(A)IT
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so WIT goes around A

blocks.note: a ship that lists leans over

annotation.surface: Americans waiting for returned tickets tilt towards the clever ones.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returns' are returned tickets; 'from US' marks waitlist as American usage.
annotation.definitionFit: A waitlist is the queue of people hoping a place or ticket becomes free.

entries.clue: Show fear, accepting millions in sort of bet (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so TREBLE takes M inside
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places M inside TREBLE, restating the same instruction from M's side

blocks.note: a treble is a bet on three races

annotation.surface: A gambler shaking at the thought of winning millions on a bet.
annotation.walkthrough: A treble is a bet linking three selections; M goes after TRE.
annotation.definitionFit: Shaking is the physical sign of fear, so to tremble is to show it.

entries.clue: Temperature OK, but not at first snug (5)

indicatorNotes.not at first: 'not at first' means missing what comes first, so the opening letter goes

annotation.surface: The room temperature is fine, though it didn't feel cosy at first.
annotation.walkthrough: OK gives RIGHT, which then loses its R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a snug fit and a tight fit both leave no room.

entries.clue: Friend capturing beginning of drama in Roman Catholic exam (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another: ACT I sits inside RC

blocks.note: Act I is how a play begins

annotation.surface: A friend takes a Catholic school drama exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of drama' tempts you to take D; it is ACT I, the first act.
annotation.definitionFit: A practical is an exam where you carry out tasks rather than write.

entries.clue: Ready to agree morning permit (8)

annotation.surface: Happy to sign off on a morning permit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Permit' looks like a noun; it is the verb, enable.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is willing to go along with things.

entries.clue: Motoring offence with nothing on fine received for overindulging (5-7)

indicatorNotes.received: SPEEDING receives the other letters inside

blocks.note: f = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: A driver caught speeding, getting a fine on top of nothing much.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing on fine' is three separate pieces read in order, all tucked inside the offence after its first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Spoon-feeding is giving someone too much help, overindulging them.

entries.clue: Environmental concern — extraordinary ability around company in this place (9)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so ESP encircles CO

annotation.surface: A green company boasts of its remarkable talents here.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Environmental concern' reads as a worry about the environment; here 'concern' is the subject matter, and 'concern' can also mean a company.
annotation.definitionFit: The ecosphere is the region of the planet where life exists, the whole environment.

entries.clue: English still not finished limiting European plan (8)

indicatorNotes.limiting: to limit is to set bounds on both sides, so INER hems in E

annotation.surface: An English Eurosceptic's unfinished scheme to curb Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' is the adjective, motionless, not the adverb meaning 'even now'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to engineer an outcome is to contrive or plan it.

entries.clue: Deception in origins of old articles skewering Hard Times (4)

indicatorNotes.origins of: take the first letter of each word
indicatorNotes.skewering: OA runs through H and X, sitting between them

annotation.surface: A fake exposed in the old pieces that ran through Dickens's Hard Times.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard Times' pretends to be the Dickens novel; it is H and X.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hoax is a trick meant to deceive.

entries.clue: I note Christian Union mostly unable to shift a lot of old books (10)

blocks.note: CU = Christian Union, a student society
UNABLE, mostly: its last letter goes
taken as written; joins UNABL to be shifted

annotation.surface: A student noting that the Christian Union can't move its heap of old books.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' is fodder, not an article: UNABL plus A is rearranged to NABULA.
annotation.definitionFit: Incunabula are books printed before 1501, in the infancy of printing.

entries.clue: Burlesque act to become suddenly popular (4,3)

blocks.note: a burlesque act mimics someone for comic effect
a trend that takes off suddenly catches on

annotation.surface: A comic sketch that suddenly becomes a hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burlesque' tempts you towards striptease; it means parody here.
annotation.definitionFit: A take-off mimics something for laughs; to take off is to succeed suddenly.

entries.clue: Broadway comedian lots finally dismissed, making silly point? (9)

indicatorNotes.finally dismissed: the final letter is sent away

blocks.note: W.C. Fields, who starred in the Ziegfeld Follies

annotation.surface: A comedian makes a daft remark as many in the audience walk out.
annotation.walkthrough: Silly point is a cricket fielding position right next to the batsman, so the player there is a fieldsman; the question mark flags this definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: silly point is one fielding position, so the player there is a fieldsman.

entries.clue: Support succeeded, restraining skittish horse? On the contrary (7)

indicatorNotes.restraining: one piece holds the other inside
indicatorNotes.On the contrary: swap the roles: the horse holds S, not the other way round

blocks.note: a bolter is a horse that runs off

annotation.surface: A rider props up a nervous horse and gets it under control.
annotation.walkthrough: Read straight, S restrains the horse; 'on the contrary' reverses that, so BOLTER holds S: BOL(S)TER.
annotation.definitionFit: To bolster is to support; a bolster is also a long supporting pillow.

entries.clue: Lit charge, scrambled — not being this? (9)

annotation.definition: Lit charge, scrambled — not being this?
annotation.surface: Someone who lit a fuse then scrambled away, the opposite of sluggish.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: anyone who charges off and scrambles is not being lethargic.
annotation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish, the opposite of lighting out and scrambling.

entries.clue: Church father tucking into more mature edible leaves (4,5)

indicatorNotes.tucking into: CE and PA tuck themselves inside RIPER

annotation.surface: A priest tucking into a salad of older greens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' and 'edible leaves' paint a meal; the leaves are sheets of paper.
annotation.definitionFit: Rice paper is thin edible sheets used in cooking.

entries.clue: Forgetfulness? The writer’s penning note in China, India etc (7)

indicatorNotes.penning: to pen is to shut in a pen, so ME shuts N inside
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another: M(N)E sits inside ASIA

annotation.surface: A travel writer jotting a note somewhere in Asia, then forgetting it.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' linking pieces: the writer is penning a note; M(N)E then goes inside ASIA after the A.
annotation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory; the question mark marks it as an extreme kind of forgetfulness.

entries.clue: Mathematical method a focus of wage negotiations? Ring us about company’s ultimatum initially (12,8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so CALL goes around CU
indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so take the first letter of each of the two words

blocks.note: a pay differential is the gap between wage levels
first letters of Company’s and Ultimatum

annotation.surface: A union negotiator: call us about the company's final offer.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half defines by example: pay differentials between grades are a classic bargaining point. 'Initially' covers two words, not just 'ultimatum'.
annotation.definitionFit: Differential calculus is the branch of maths dealing with rates of change.

entries.clue: Incline to go the wrong way about rescue vessel where surfing is riskier? (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so DNET goes around ARK

blocks.note: Noah's ark, which rescued the animals

annotation.surface: A lifeboat heading the wrong way to a beach where the waves are dangerous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surfing' is the internet kind, not the beach kind the rescue vessel suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: The darknet is a hidden part of the internet where browsing carries more risk.

entries.clue: It turns up in a sound from duck, mostly on water (7)

indicatorNotes.turns up: in a down clue, IT turned upside down reads TI
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another: TI sits inside QUAC

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned up

annotation.surface: A duck's call pops up across the water.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turns up' reads bottom to top, so IT becomes TI.
annotation.definitionFit: Aquatic means living or happening on or in water.

entries.clue: Vote to replace contents of audio program for Nasa (6)

indicatorNotes.to replace contents of: POLL takes the place of the inside letters

blocks.note: AUDIO with its contents, UDI, removed

annotation.surface: Voting to swap out a sound program for the space agency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Program' looks like software beside 'audio'; it is the American spelling of programme, the space programme.
annotation.definitionFit: Apollo was NASA's programme that landed men on the Moon.

entries.clue: Notices a wide source of oscillation (6)

annotation.surface: An engineer notices a wide swing in a signal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notices' looks like a noun; it is the verb, sees.
annotation.definitionFit: A seesaw goes up and down, back and forth.

entries.clue: Essentially a means to identify component of meteor shower (7)

annotation.surface: An astronomer on how to spot a shooting star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' pretends to be a hedge; it gives PER SE.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by part: each meteor of the August Perseid shower is itself a Perseid.

entries.clue: Copper covered in grain ground by assistant? I’ll take the blame (3,5)

indicatorNotes.covered in: something covered in flour has it all over the outside, so MEAL wraps round CU

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A policeman covered in flour at the mill confesses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is the element, not the policeman the surface suggests. 'By' joins MEA(CU)L to PA.
annotation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'my fault'.

entries.clue: Simple cut? The thing has value (5)

indicatorNotes.cut: MERE is cut short, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: Is a simple haircut worth anything?
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'cut' makes it look like a haircut; it cuts MERE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: merit and value both mean worth.

entries.clue: Plan that is cracked open by introduction of great chatterer (6)

indicatorNotes.cracked open by: a thing cracked open by an intruder has it wedged inside, so G splits MAP

blocks.note: to map out is to plan

annotation.surface: A scheme broken open by a loudmouth who can't stop talking.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue order suggests 'that is' is broken open too; only the plan is cracked, and 'that is' simply follows.
annotation.definitionFit: Magpies are noisy birds, and a magpie is a chatterbox.

entries.clue: You are almost ready for ancient language (4)

indicatorNotes.almost: DUE is not quite complete, losing its last letter

blocks.note: DUE (ready, expected) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone nearly prepared to study an old tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: UR is textspeak, a newer abbreviation than most in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language of Pakistan and India with a long literary history.

entries.clue: Hawaiian building back to front in Hawaiian allotment (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is inside the following words

annotation.surface: A Hawaiian shed built the wrong way round on a local allotment.
annotation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented garden plot, British style. The second 'Hawaiian' is the one that hides the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: lanai is the Hawaiian name for a roofed veranda.

entries.clue: Power to secure bishop as perfect husband (2,5)

indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure is to hold fast, so MIGHT holds RR inside

blocks.note: RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

annotation.surface: A powerful woman landing a bishop as her ideal man.
annotation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, which is where RR comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the ideal man to marry.

entries.clue: Impudent relative suppressing American ailment (9)

indicatorNotes.suppressing: PERT and SIS hold US down between them

annotation.surface: A cheeky sister hiding her American illness.
annotation.walkthrough: The American is held between the two outer words, cheek on one side and sister on the other. Pertussis is whooping cough.
annotation.definitionFit: Pertussis is the medical name for whooping cough.

entries.clue: I note cogent works describing individual development (11)

indicatorNotes.works: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A reviewer praising persuasive books about how a person grows up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun, books; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Ontogenetic relates to ontogeny, the development of an individual organism.

entries.clue: Widely-distributed leaflet regarded as tool (8,3)

blocks.note: a circular is a leaflet sent to many

annotation.surface: A flyer being viewed as a useful instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regarded' is the past tense of see, SAW.
annotation.definitionFit: A circular saw is a power tool with a rotating toothed disc.
